newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's Imperial Oil posts record 1996 profit.
newsitem.headline: Canada's Imperial Oil posts record 1996 profit.

text.p: Imperial Oil Ltd., Canada's biggest energy company, reported record 1996 earnings and revenues on Wednesday, spurred by strong oil and natural gas prices and a huge tax refund.
Net earnings at Toronto-based Imperial rose to C$786 million ($582 million) or C$4.47 ($3.31) a share last year from C$514 million ($380 million) or C$2.67 ($1.98) a share in 1995.
Revenues climbed to C$10.5 billion ($7.8 billion) from C$9.6 billion ($7.1 billion) the year before.
In the fourth quarter, Imperial's earnings rose to C$198 million ($147 million) or C$1.24 (92 cents) a share from the year earlier C$93 million ($69 million) or C49 cents (36 cents) a share.
Imperial also benefited from a C$840 million ($622 million) tax refund from the Canadian government last March, which resulted in a C$322 million ($238 million) gain to earnings.
That was partly offset by C$33 million ($24 million) in after-tax expenses for the debt redemption.
Imperial's strong results followed sharply higher earnings last week from competitor Suncor Inc. in what was expected to be a windfall 1996 for Canada's integrated oil sector.
Imperial produces oil and gas in western Canada and operates Canada's most extensive refining and marketing business. The company is 69.6 percent-owned by U.S.-based Exxon Corp..
